name: Sildenafil Pivotal Trials
aliases: Sildenafil Study Group dose-response and dose-escalation studies
question: Does as-needed oral sildenafil improve erectile function over placebo in men with erectile dysfunction of organic, psychogenic or mixed cause?

arms.label: Oral sildenafil, fixed 25, 50 or 100 mg or flexible dosing from 50 mg

design.population: 861 men aged 18 or older with erectile dysfunction for at least 6 months at 37 US centers, in a stable relationship with a female partner (70% organic, 11% psychogenic, 18% mixed cause).
design.description: Two sequential double-blind placebo-controlled randomized studies

verdictNote: Both studies favored sildenafil on penetration and maintenance scores; efficacy rested on patient self-report.
takeaway: Oral sildenafil versus placebo in 861 men with erectile dysfunction: in a 24-week fixed-dose study, IIEF penetration and erection-maintenance scores rose with 25, 50 and 100 mg; in a 12-week flexible-dose study, 69% versus 22% of intercourse attempts succeeded (P<0.001).

reports.label: Dose-response and dose-escalation studies
reports.citation: Goldstein I, Lue TF, Padma-Nathan H, et al. "Oral Sildenafil in the Treatment of Erectile Dysfunction." *N Engl J Med.* 1998;338(20):1397-1404. doi:10.1056/NEJM199805143382001
reports.followUp: 24 weeks (dose-response study); 12 weeks (dose-escalation study); 32-week open-label extension in 225 men

results.measure: Mean end-of-treatment score, scale 1-5 (24 weeks); sildenafil 25, 50 and 100 mg
results.note: Baseline 2.0, 1.9, 2.0 versus 2.1 for placebo; increases of 60%, 84% and 100% versus 5%. Analyzed n=96, 105, 101 versus 199.

results.measure: Mean end-of-treatment score, scale 1-5 (24 weeks); sildenafil 25, 50 and 100 mg
results.note: Baseline 1.4, 1.5, 1.7 versus 1.7 for placebo; increases of 121%, 133% and 130% versus 24%.
Baseline 2.0 versus 2.1; increase 95% versus 10%; n=138 in each group.
Baseline 1.5 versus 1.6; increase 140% versus 13%; n=137 versus 138.

results.measure: Percentage of all attempts at intercourse that were successful, last 4 weeks, event log (dose-escalation study)
results.note: Mean successful attempts in the last 4 weeks: 5.9 versus 1.5 (P<0.001). Analyzed n=157 versus 154.

results.measure: Mean domain score, possible range 1-30 (dose-escalation study)
results.note: Analyzed n=136 versus 134. The domain score also rose with dose in the dose-response study (P<0.001); the paper gives no values in text.

results.endpoint: Global efficacy question: improved erections, dose-response study
results.measure: Proportion answering yes at 24 weeks; sildenafil 25, 50 and 100 mg

results.endpoint: Global efficacy question: improved erections, dose-escalation study
results.measure: Proportion answering yes at 12 weeks, among men who responded to the question

results.endpoint: Erections hard enough for intercourse (grade 3 or 4), dose-response study
results.measure: Proportion of men with such erections during the last 4 weeks of event-log review; sildenafil 25, 50 and 100 mg
results.note: 80% of grade 3 and 94% of grade 4 erections resulted in successful intercourse.

results.endpoint: IIEF question 3 by cause, dose-escalation study
results.measure: Mean end-of-treatment score, scale 1-5, by investigator-assigned cause
results.note: Subgroups were small; question 4 was significant in all three causes (P<0.001, <0.001, 0.005).

results.measure: Between-group comparison of mean domain score
results.note: No significant difference; orgasmic-function, intercourse-satisfaction and overall-satisfaction domain scores were higher with sildenafil (P<0.001).

harms.label: Headache
harms.note: Adverse effects listed are those occurring in 5% or more of any treatment group; extension (open-label, n=225): 28 (12%).

harms.label: Visual disturbance (change in color hue or brightness)
harms.note: Usually mild, lasting a few minutes to a few hours after dosing; extension: 9 (4%).

harms.label: Discontinuation for treatment-related adverse effects
harms.note: Open-label extension: 4/225 (2%) withdrew for treatment-related adverse effects.

delivery.label: Dosing instruction
delivery.value: One dose about one hour before planned sexual activity, not more than once daily

delivery.label: Dose-response study (fixed dose)
delivery.note: 24 weeks; each dose was three tablets from one blister-pack row; 465/532 (87%) completed.

delivery.label: Dose-escalation study (flexible dose)
delivery.note: 12 weeks; at each visit the dose could be doubled or reduced by 50% according to response and adverse effects; 307/329 (93%) completed.

delivery.label: Final dose after 12 weeks (dose-escalation study)
delivery.note: Corresponding proportions are given for the placebo group.

delivery.label: Completion of the assigned treatment period
Open-label extension
delivery.value: 225 men entered a 32-week extension of sildenafil; 207/225 (92%) completed it

reports.label: Pooled safety analysis
reports.citation: Morales A, Gingell C, Collins M, et al. "Clinical Safety of Oral Sildenafil Citrate (VIAGRA) in the Treatment of Erectile Dysfunction." *Int J Impot Res.* 1998;10(2):69-73. doi:10.1038/sj.ijir.3900354
reports.followUp: Double-blind treatment up to 6 months; open-label extension up to 1 year

harms.label: Headache, all causes
harms.note: Pooled double-blind studies: 2722 sildenafil and 1552 placebo patients.

harms.label: Discontinuation for adverse events, all causes
harms.note: In the open-label extension studies, 90% completed long-term treatment and 2% withdrew for adverse events.

reports.label: Published correction
reports.citation: "Oral Sildenafil in the Treatment of Erectile Dysfunction" [correction]. *N Engl J Med.* 1998;339(1):59. doi:10.1056/NEJM199807023390121

delivery.label: Corrections
delivery.value: The abstract's first sentence reads "inhibitor of cyclic guanosine monophosphate hydrolysis"; the Results sentence on baseline differences refers to the dose-escalation study, not the dose-response study

reports.label: Long-term extension studies
reports.citation: Steers W, Guay AT, Leriche A, et al. "Assessment of the Efficacy and Safety of Viagra (Sildenafil Citrate) in Men with Erectile Dysfunction during Long-Term Treatment." *Int J Impot Res.* 2001;13(5):261-267. doi:10.1038/sj.ijir.3900714
reports.followUp: 36 or 52 weeks of open-label treatment in 1008 men

results.measure: Proportion answering that treatment improved their erections (open-label extension, n=1008)
results.note: Four flexible-dose (25-100 mg) open-label extension studies; no comparison group.
